main_text.l: gus ab aqua proveniens ibi dominatur: ex quo fit,
ut flatus Austrini calor vix in pontum penetret. At-
qui provenit ibi calor quidā intrò coactus per ἀν-
τιπερίστασιν[?] (quasi dicas, contrariorum circumstan-
tiam) à frigore undique circumambiente, & Borea
prævalente. Itaque talis calor quando vi circumfusi
frigoris excitatur, tum ros producitur.
Quæ sunt causæ nivis?
1. Causa materialis, vapores. Eadem plane mate-
ria est nivis, quæ & primæ: verum nivis materia
altius subvehitur.
2. Causa formalis: Eodem pacto procreatur nix,
quo pruina. Etenim proportio & ἀναλογία[?] magna
est nivis cum pruina, sicut & pluviæ cum rore. Nix
namq; & pruina gignuntur tantum tempore ac loc-
is frigidis, sicut ros & pruina tempore ac locis sub-
calidis. Hæc autem, ut rectius iudicemus de causa
nivis formali, sunt observanda discrimina: Pluvia
sublimiore loco & ex crassiore provenit materia
(nempe à magnis nubibus) eademq; longiore temporis
spacio collecta: ros vero loco humiliore
ex materia tenui, & tanquam ex nebulis, & sursum cue-
cta unius diei spacio. Ad eundem modum nix quoq;
loco sublimiore ex materia corpulenta & paula-
tim collecta procreatur: pruina vero loco
hu-miliore ex materia exili & celeri-
ter è terris educta.

page.notes: Page number at the head right is faint and read as 313 with doubt. Greek words ἀντιπερίστασιν and ἀναλογία are uncertain in their accents and letters. The two marginal notes "Libro I." and "cap. II." are small and partly rubbed. Show-through from the other side is visible in the lower margins and is left out. The top-left fragment "gus" is the end of a word from the previous line of the printed page and is kept as a fragment.
